title: Reduce streaming token latency: optimize token loop, flush cadence, backpressure, kernel scheduling, and KV cache batching
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: reduce tail and median latency for streaming token generation observed in production canaries and customer reports (INC-1023). Summary: refactor token emission loop to reduce syscall/backpressure overhead, move flush cadence logic into the batching layer, add cooperative backpressure signal between scheduler and batcher, improve kernel scheduling heuristics to prioritize low-latency microbatches, and enable KV-cache-aware batching heuristics to avoid redundant KV loads. This change touches the serving runtime token path, scheduling, and KV cache. Details: 1) token loop rewrite reduces context switches by coalescing user-space flush requests into an atomic enqueue then single wakeup; 2) flush cadence becomes adaptive based on batch occupancy and latency SLOs instead of fixed timers; 3) backpressure propagation added so slow downstream consumers slow upstream batching at the socket boundary; 4) scheduler now scores microbatches by expected token count and KV cache hit probability and selects kernels that reduce per-token latency for short sequences; 5) KV cache batching deduplicates concurrent KV lookups and stages warm entries into a shared fast-path to avoid rematerialization. Testing and rollout: unit + integration tests added, perf harness with 72h canary in us-west-2, staged rollout (1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automatic rollback on QoS regression. Results: p50 token latency -15%, p95 -28%, p99 -42% across our internal canary for chat workloads; token throughput throughput unchanged or slightly improved. No API changes. Related: ENG-2147, ENG-2199, references to earlier streaming PR series for flush/backpressure improvements.
